papers.title: MicroNucML enables machine learning-based micronuclei segmentation and micronuclei-nuclei association.
papers.abstract: Micronuclei (MN) are structures containing small DNA fragments that arise from mitotic errors or failed DNA repair and serve as markers of genome instability. MN are typically quantified manually or with threshold methods, which can be tedious and inaccurate, leading to variable success and throughput. By employing a two-phase labeling approach that uses polygon and brush segmentation, along with SAM2-based refinement, we developed a high-quality MN segmentation tool. Data augmentation capturing heterogeneity in image quality and color diversity enabled us to train a generalizable Mask region-
papers.summary: This paper introduces MicroNucML, a machine-learning tool for automated segmentation of micronuclei (MN) and their association with nuclei, addressing limitations of manual or threshold-based methods. The tool uses a two-phase labeling approach with SAM2-based refinement and data augmentation to achieve high-quality, generalizable segmentation across diverse image conditions.

papers.title: Decoding cancer with artificial intelligence: Transforming research, diagnosis, and therapy with future insights.
papers.abstract: Cancer remains one of the leading global health burdens, with increasing complexity in genomic, imaging, and clinical datasets presenting significant challenges for effective management. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a powerful tool to address these challenges by enabling pattern recognition, knowledge integration, and data-driven decision-making. This review highlights recent advances in the application of AI across cancer research, diagnosis, and therapy. In research, AI accelerates drug discovery and repurposing, enhances genomic data interpretation, and facilitates biomarker
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial intelligence is transforming cancer research, diagnosis, and therapy by enabling pattern recognition and data-driven decision-making across complex genomic, imaging, and clinical datasets. It highlights AI's role in accelerating drug discovery, improving genomic interpretation, and facilitating biomarker identification, while also addressing future opportunities and challenges.

papers.title: Improving RNA Secondary Structure Prediction Through Expanded Training Data.
papers.abstract: In recent years, deep-learning has revolutionized protein structure prediction, achieving remarkable speed and accuracy. RNA structure prediction, however, has lagged behind. Although several methods have shown moderate success in predicting RNA secondary and tertiary structures, none have reached the accuracy observed with contemporary protein models. The lack of success of these RNA structure prediction models has been proposed to be due to limited high-quality structural information that can be used as training data. To probe this proposed limitation, we developed a large and diverse datase
papers.summary: This paper investigates whether limited training data is the bottleneck for RNA secondary structure prediction by developing a large and diverse dataset. The work aims to improve prediction accuracy through expanded training data, addressing a key gap compared to protein structure prediction.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Identification of Survival-Associated CpG Biomarkers in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is an exceptionally aggressive cancer with a 5-year survival rate of less than 10%, driven by late-stage diagnosis, limited treatment options, and a lack of reliable biomarkers for early detection and prognosis. In this study, we integrated DNA methylation data from TCGA and ICGC cohorts, categorizing samples based on survival time, and identified 688 differentially methylated CpG sites, along with 224 CpG biomarkers significantly associated with patient survival through statistical and machine learning-based analyses. We developed a random forest model
papers.summary: This study analyzed DNA methylation data from TCGA and ICGC cohorts to identify CpG biomarkers associated with survival in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Using statistical and machine learning methods, they found 688 differentially methylated CpG sites and 224 survival-associated biomarkers, and developed a random forest model for prognosis.

papers.title: From rules to foundation models: a comprehensive review of machine learning approaches for siRNA design.
papers.abstract: Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) are a clinically validated therapeutic modality with eight FDA-approved drugs, yet designing effective siRNAs remains computationally challenging due to complex dependencies on sequence composition, thermodynamic properties, target-site accessibility, and off-target interactions. Over two decades, computational approaches have evolved from empirical heuristics to deep learning systems integrating physical priors with learned representations. We review the complete landscape of machine learning methods for siRNA design, spanning classical scoring rules, pretraine
papers.summary: This review comprehensively surveys machine learning approaches for siRNA design, tracing their evolution from empirical rules to modern foundation models that integrate physical priors with learned representations. It highlights the ongoing computational challenges in capturing sequence, thermodynamic, and off-target dependencies, and provides a structured overview of methods spanning classical scoring to deep learning.

papers.title: Machine learning provides individualized prediction of outcomes after first complete remission without allo-HSCT consolidation in adult acute myeloid leukemia-A HARMONY study.
papers.abstract: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) is a curative treatment option for a significant proportion of patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and it is generally recommended when the relapse risk without allo-HSCT outweighs the estimated non-relapse mortality significantly. While current recommendations for allo-HSCT are based on risk groups, there is considerable heterogeneity within these individual categories. We analyzed 2550 intensively treated AML patients aged 18-70 with cytogenetic and next-generation sequencing data from the HARMONY Alliance database, who d
papers.summary: This study used machine learning on data from 2550 AML patients to develop individualized predictions of outcomes after achieving first complete remission without undergoing allogeneic stem cell transplantation. The model aims to refine transplant recommendations by accounting for heterogeneity within current risk groups, potentially improving personalized treatment decisions.

papers.title: Gene-level complexity explains genome-wide variation in the distribution of fitness effects.
papers.abstract: The distribution of fitness effects (DFE)-describing how harmful, neutral, or beneficial new mutations are-is central to understanding how populations evolve. Although the DFE varies across genomes and species, it remains unclear which aspects of genomic organization drive this variation. Here, we inferred gene-level selective constraints across the genomes of Mus musculus castaneus, Drosophila melanogaster and Saccharomyces cerevisiae using a combination of population genetics and machine learning trained on diverse gene features. Many gene features were predictive of selective constraint, wi
papers.summary: This study investigates what drives variation in the distribution of fitness effects (DFE) across genomes by inferring gene-level selective constraints in mice, fruit flies, and yeast using population genetics and machine learning. They found that many gene features predict selective constraint, and that gene-level complexity—likely reflecting pleiotropy or functional connectivity—explains a large portion of genome-wide DFE variation. This provides a mechanistic link between genomic organization and the evolutionary fate of new mutations.

papers.title: DyAb: sequence-based antibody design and property prediction in a low-data regime.
papers.abstract: Protein therapeutic design and property prediction are frequently hampered by data scarcity. Here we propose a model, DyAb, that addresses these issues by leveraging a pair-wise representation to predict differences in binding affinity, rather than absolute values. DyAb is built on top of a pre-trained protein language model and achieves a Spearman rank correlation of up to 0.85 on binding affinity prediction across monoclonal antibodies targeting three different antigens (EGFR, IL-6, and an internal target), given as few as 100 training data. We employ DyAb in two design contexts: as a rankin
papers.summary: DyAb is a new antibody design and property prediction model that predicts differences in binding affinity rather than absolute values, enabling accurate ranking with as few as 100 training examples. Built on a pre-trained protein language model, it achieves high Spearman correlations (up to 0.85) across antibodies targeting multiple antigens, making it useful for therapeutic design in data-scarce settings.

papers.title: HelixCross - Design and development of an AI-powered cross-examination simulation for forensic expert testimony training.
papers.abstract: Forensic testimony is where science meets the courtroom, and it is one of the critical forensic skills taught largely by apprenticeship. An examiner who overstates a match, mishandles a probability, or cannot support a method under direct or cross-examination can weaken the evidence in precisely the cases that rely on it. Yet in most forensic laboratories, testimony preparation remains largely informal, mentor-dependent, and unscalable. Consequently, many practitioners first face rigorous cross-examination at trial. To address this gap, HelixCross, an alpha-stage, publicly accessible, prompt-e
papers.summary: HelixCross is an AI-powered simulation tool designed to train forensic experts in cross-examination testimony, addressing a gap where such training is often informal and mentor-dependent. The tool uses prompt engineering to simulate rigorous cross-examination scenarios, providing scalable and accessible practice for forensic practitioners.

papers.title: A computational framework integrating a protein language model with alchemical simulation for gain-of-function enzyme design.
papers.abstract: Engineering enzymes with enhanced activity and stability is a central goal of biotechnology, yet the inherent trade-off between optimizing global protein fitness and specific substrate binding affinity poses a significant challenge. Here, we present ESM-FEP, a computational framework that synergistically integrates a fine-tuned protein language model with alchemical free energy perturbation (FEP) to overcome this limitation. Our workflow employs a parameter-efficient fine-tuned ESM-2 model to perform high-throughput saturation mutagenesis, rapidly identifying mutations that preserve protein fi
papers.summary: The authors introduce ESM-FEP, a computational framework that combines a fine-tuned protein language model with alchemical free energy perturbation to design enzymes with enhanced activity and stability. This approach addresses the trade-off between global protein fitness and substrate binding affinity by using the language model for high-throughput saturation mutagenesis screening and FEP for precise binding affinity evaluation. The framework is presented as a tool for gain-of-function enzyme engineering.

papers.title: aiDIVA - hybrid AI for rare disease diagnostics using evidence-based, machine learning and language models.
papers.abstract: Genome sequencing enables accurate detection of genetic variants and is transforming rare disease diagnostics. While data generation is scalable, prioritization and clinical interpretation remain challenging, often requiring expert manual classification. AI-driven decision support systems are therefore needed to assist in causal variant identification or to fully automate large-scale re-analysis of unsolved cases. Existing tools often estimate variant impact on protein function, but few integrate genomic, phenotypic, and clinical annotation data for diagnosis. We present aiDIVA, an ensemble-AI
papers.summary: aiDIVA is a hybrid AI system that integrates genomic, phenotypic, and clinical data to prioritize causal variants in rare disease diagnostics. It combines evidence-based rules, machine learning, and language models to improve variant interpretation and enable automated re-analysis of unsolved cases.

papers.title: Pooled two-cohort MRI body composition phenotyping with open-source deep learning.
papers.abstract: Body mass index fails to capture variation in fat and muscle distribution that determines metabolic health and disease risk. MRI enables radiation-free quantification of regional body composition, yet scalable open-source tools applied in pooled cohorts with differing acquisition protocols have been lacking.
papers.summary: This paper presents an open-source deep learning tool for quantifying regional body composition from MRI scans, validated across two cohorts with different imaging protocols. It addresses the need for scalable, radiation-free phenotyping beyond BMI, enabling pooled analyses of fat and muscle distribution for metabolic health research.

papers.title: Machine-Learning-Assisted Impedance Component Analysis Enables Standardizable Surface Protein Analysis of Extracellular Vesicles Using Engineered Nanovesicles.
papers.abstract: Characterizing surface protein heterogeneity on extracellular vesicles remains challenging but essential for understanding their biological functions and clinical applications. Here, this study introduces an integrated platform that combines engineered cell-derived nanovesicles, used as model standards with controlled surface protein states, and machine learning-optimized impedance spectroscopy. Cell-derived nanovesicles with defined surface protein densities are generated by extruding HeLa cells expressing 1, 3, or 9 copies of amyloid-β 42, establishing a series of reference vesicles with pre
papers.summary: This study introduces a platform combining engineered cell-derived nanovesicles with defined surface protein densities and machine learning-optimized impedance spectroscopy to enable standardizable analysis of extracellular vesicle surface proteins. The approach addresses the challenge of characterizing surface protein heterogeneity, offering a reproducible method for clinical and biological applications.

papers.title: Learning precise segmentation of neurofibrillary tangles from rapid manual point annotations.
papers.abstract: Accumulation of abnormal tau protein into neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs) is a pathologic hallmark of Alzheimer disease (AD). Accurate detection of NFTs in tissue samples can reveal relationships with clinical, demographic, and genetic features through deep phenotyping. However, expert manual analysis is time-consuming, subject to observer variability, and cannot handle the data amounts generated by modern imaging. We present a scalable, open-source, deep-learning approach to quantify NFT burden in digital whole slide images (WSIs) of post-mortem human brain tissue. To achieve this, we develope
papers.summary: This paper presents an open-source deep-learning method for segmenting neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs) in whole slide images of Alzheimer's disease brain tissue, trained using rapid manual point annotations rather than time-consuming pixel-level tracing. The approach enables scalable and consistent quantification of NFT burden, facilitating deep phenotyping studies that link pathology to clinical and genetic data.

papers.title: scProtoTransformer: Scalable reference mapping across molecules, cells, and donors.
papers.abstract: The rapid accumulation of single-cell data has made it possible to comprehensively characterize biological systems at molecular, cellular, and donor levels. However, scalable reference mapping across different resolutions remains a major challenge in current research. Here, we propose scProtoTransformer, a prototype-based Transformer architecture designed to achieve scalable reference mapping across molecular, cell, and donor levels. scProtoTransformer introduces a knowledge-guided prototype tokenizer that projects gene expression into biologically interpretable pathway prototypes, effectively
papers.summary: scProtoTransformer is a new Transformer-based method that enables scalable mapping of single-cell data across molecular, cellular, and donor levels by projecting gene expression into interpretable pathway prototypes. This approach addresses a key challenge in integrating and comparing single-cell datasets at multiple biological resolutions, potentially improving cross-study analyses.

papers.title: Programmable protein degraders enable selective knockdown of pathogenic β-catenin subpopulations in vitro and in vivo.
papers.abstract: Aberrant activation of Wnt signaling results in unregulated accumulation of cytosolic β-catenin, which subsequently enters the nucleus and promotes transcription of genes that contribute to cellular proliferation and malignancy. Here, we sought to eliminate pathogenic β-catenin from the cytosol using designer ubiquibodies (uAbs), chimeric proteins composed of an E3 ubiquitin ligase and a target-binding domain that redirect intracellular proteins to the proteasome for degradation. To accelerate uAb development, we leveraged a protein language model-driven algorithm called SaLT&PepPr to computat
papers.summary: This study presents programmable protein degraders (ubiquibodies) that selectively eliminate pathogenic cytosolic β-catenin, a key driver of Wnt signaling-related cancers, without affecting nuclear pools. Using a protein language model-driven design, the authors achieved targeted knockdown in vitro and in vivo, offering a new therapeutic strategy for β-catenin-driven malignancies.

papers.title: iDCF: Interpretable deconvolution of cell fractions via biologically-informed deep learning using scRNA-seq data.
papers.abstract: Precise resolution of cellular heterogeneity within complex tissues is fundamental to deciphering disease etiologies from bulk transcriptomic profiles. While computational deconvolution offers a scalable alternative, current deep learning methods predominantly operate as "black boxes," neglecting the structural constraints of biological laws. This reliance on purely data-driven feature extraction often yields biologically incoherent predictions and limited mechanistic interpretability. iDCF (Interpretable Deconvolution of Cell Fractions) is a novel framework that enforces biological topology o
papers.summary: iDCF is a new deep learning framework for deconvolving cell type fractions from bulk transcriptomics data. Unlike existing black-box methods, it incorporates biological structural constraints to improve the biological coherence and interpretability of predictions, offering a more reliable tool for studying cellular heterogeneity in complex tissues.

papers.title: Deciphering the comprehensive relationship between 5' UTR and 3' UTR sequences with deep learning.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in mRNA therapeutics have driven further research on the untranslated regions (UTRs) of mRNA. However, prior studies have mainly focused on either the 5' or 3' UTR individually. Increasing evidence suggests potential cooperative effects between these two regions, which remain largely unexplored in computational studies.
papers.summary: This paper introduces a deep learning approach to jointly analyze 5' and 3' untranslated regions (UTRs) of mRNA, capturing their cooperative effects on gene expression. By modeling both UTRs together, the method provides a more comprehensive understanding of regulatory sequences, which could improve the design of mRNA therapeutics.

papers.title: Challenges and opportunities in type III secretion system effector prediction.
papers.abstract: Type III secretion system effectors (T3SEs) are small bacterial proteins with big biological roles. They act as central molecular mediators of interactions between Gram-negative bacteria and eukaryotic hosts, spanning pathogenic, symbiotic and environmental contexts. Over the past three decades, T3SE discovery has progressed from genome-independent experimental assays to an expanding landscape of computational prediction methods. Early in silico approaches formalized empirically defined protein N-terminal properties into feature-engineered machine-learning models, followed by deep-learning met
papers.summary: This review discusses the evolution and current state of computational methods for predicting Type III secretion system effectors (T3SEs), from early feature-engineered machine-learning models to modern deep-learning approaches. It highlights the challenges in accurate prediction and outlines opportunities for future methodological improvements, emphasizing the importance of T3SEs as mediators of bacteria-host interactions.

papers.title: Development of a Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP)-Interpretable Model for Cardiovascular Risk Stratification in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Implications of MDA-Modified Protein Adducts and Autoantibodies.
papers.abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is the leading cause of mortality in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). This study explores the two-hit oxidative-immune hypothesis by evaluating malondialdehyde (MDA)-modified protein (MDA-protein) adducts and their corresponding autoantibodies for precise and fair CAD severity stratification and classification. Novel MDA-peptide epitopes (apolipoprotein B-100 (ApoB-100), fibronectin (FINC), and complement C4A/C4B (C4A/C4B)) were identified via proteomics, and plasma levels of MDA, adducts, and autoantibodies were measured in 165 Taiwanese T2DM patients. Multivaria
papers.summary: This study develops a SHAP-interpretable machine learning model to stratify coronary artery disease severity in type 2 diabetes patients using malondialdehyde-modified protein adducts and autoantibodies. The authors identified novel MDA-peptide epitopes via proteomics and measured plasma levels in 165 patients, demonstrating the utility of oxidative-immune markers for precise CAD risk classification.

papers.title: Integrating AI and Molecular Modeling for Structural Prediction of a Closed-Pore State of the hERG Channel.
papers.abstract: The voltage-gated potassium channel hERG (Kv11.1) plays a central role in cardiac repolarisation by mediating the rapid delayed rectifier K+ current (IKr). Blockage of hERG by small molecules can lead to delayed repolarisation, QT interval prolongation, and potentially fatal arrhythmias, making the channel a critical focus in drug safety screening. Despite extensive pharmacological and electrophysiological characterization, a complete structural understanding of hERG gating remains limited by the absence of an experimentally determined closed-state structure. Here, we use AI-based structural m
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This study uses AI-based structural modeling combined with molecular dynamics to predict a closed-pore state of the hERG potassium channel, which lacks an experimentally determined structure. The resulting model provides insights into the gating mechanism and offers a valuable tool for drug safety screening, as hERG blockage is linked to cardiac arrhythmias.

papers.title: Predicting Enzyme pH Optima from Structure Using Equivariant Graph Neural Networks.
papers.abstract: Enzyme activity and stability are strongly modulated by pH, making the catalytic pH optimum (pHopt) a key parameter in enzyme development and biotechnological applications. Experimental determination of pHopt is, however, labor-intensive and time-consuming, motivating the development of accurate computational prediction methods. Here, we introduce pHoptNN, an E(n)-equivariant graph neural network designed to predict enzyme pHopt directly from three-dimensional protein structures. pHoptNN was trained on a curated data set comprising nearly 12,000 enzymes with experimentally determined pHopt val
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: The authors present pHoptNN, an equivariant graph neural network that predicts an enzyme's optimal pH directly from its 3D structure, trained on nearly 12,000 enzymes. This offers a fast computational alternative to labor-intensive experimental pH optimum determination, which is valuable for enzyme engineering and biotechnology.

papers.title: CompBio and MIRaS-a multi-omic analysis platform built on a memory-based intelligence engine.
papers.abstract: As molecular and cellular technologies have advanced, the need to analyze and interpret the resulting vast and multi-modal data into actionable intelligence has become a rate-limiting factor in scientific advancement. While traditional knowledgebase-pathway tools and LLM-based AI tools provide a degree of support in data interpretation, both exhibit known limitations. Presented here is the CompBio multi-omic analysis platform built upon Memory-based Intelligent Reasoning System (MIRaS), an associative reasoning engine grounded in episodic and semantic memory, capable of inferring biological re
papers.summary: The paper introduces CompBio, a multi-omic analysis platform powered by MIRaS, an associative reasoning engine that uses episodic and semantic memory to interpret complex biological data. It aims to overcome limitations of traditional pathway tools and LLM-based AI by enabling more context-aware inference from multi-modal datasets.

papers.title: Advances in multimodal data integration for drug efficacy prediction: Methodological evolution and clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Drug efficacy prediction remains a cornerstone of drug development and precision therapy. However, integrating heterogeneous biomedical data, including multi-omics profiles, pathological imaging, electronic health records, and pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) time-series, faces three fundamental barriers, namely cross-domain distribution shifts between preclinical and clinical data, relational mismatches between isolated vector representations and biological networks, and feature heterogeneity across disparate modalities. To address these challenges, three AI paradigms have emerged, tra
papers.summary: This review examines recent advances in multimodal data integration for drug efficacy prediction, highlighting three key challenges—cross-domain distribution shifts, relational mismatches, and feature heterogeneity—and the AI paradigms developed to address them. It discusses the methodological evolution and clinical translation of these approaches, providing a framework for understanding current progress in the field.

papers.title: GRASSP: RNA Language Model-Enhanced Graph Attention with Adaptive Gating for RNA-Small Molecule Binding Site Prediction.
papers.abstract: RNA-small molecule binding site prediction is crucial for targeted drug discovery. Sequence-based methods are efficient but often fail to capture structural dependencies between nucleotides, whereas structure-aware graph models can better represent spatial interactions but typically rely on complex structural annotations and multi-stage preprocessing pipelines. We therefore developed GRASSP, a streamlined hybrid deep learning framework that integrates pretrained RNA language model (LM) representations with adaptive graph refinement.
papers.summary: GRASSP is a new deep learning framework that predicts RNA-small molecule binding sites by combining RNA language model embeddings with graph neural networks, using adaptive gating to refine structural information without complex preprocessing. It aims to improve accuracy over sequence-only methods while remaining efficient and easy to use for drug discovery applications.

papers.title: Publisher Correction: FeatureDock for protein-ligand docking guided by physicochemical feature-based local environment learning using transformer.
papers.summary: This is a publisher correction notice for a previously published article, not a new research finding. It likely addresses minor errors in the original paper without altering its scientific conclusions.

papers.title: ESM2-Guided Context-Aware Annotation Completion Supplements Carbohydrate Metabolism Coverage in Silage Microbial Metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Functional annotation gaps limit the interpretation of carbohydrate metabolism in silage microbiomes. We developed Context-Aware Annotation Completion (CAAC), a framework integrating ESM2 embeddings, genomic-neighborhood features, three-class classification, confidence-tiered neighbor voting, and Enzyme Commission (EC)-to-KEGG Orthology (KO) mapping. CAAC was applied to 21 metagenomes from uninoculated and Lacticaseibacillus paracasei-inoculated silages sampled before ensiling and at 7 and 90 days. Five-fold cross-validation yielded an F1-macro of 84.64% for negative, positive, and hard-sequen
papers.summary: The authors developed CAAC, a framework that uses ESM2 protein language model embeddings and genomic context to predict missing enzyme annotations in silage microbial metagenomes, improving carbohydrate metabolism coverage. Applied to 21 silage metagenomes, it achieved high cross-validation performance and expanded functional annotation, offering a new tool for microbiome studies.

papers.title: PregBase: A comprehensive knowledge base for clinically relevant knowledge representation and biomarker prediction in pregnancy.
papers.abstract: Pregnancy complications are a leading cause of maternal and neonatal mortality worldwide. Understanding their underlying mechanisms is hindered by dispersed evidence across thousands of studies and complex biological interactions. We present PregBase, a comprehensive knowledge base for pregnancy research comprising automated extraction, validation, and exploration. PregBase was constructed by utilising large language models (LLMs) to extract relationships from literature; 13 LLMs were benchmarked across seven prompting strategies, with ensemble shuffle prompting outperforming single-strategy a
papers.summary: PregBase is a new knowledge base for pregnancy research that uses large language models to automatically extract and validate relationships from the scientific literature. The authors benchmarked 13 LLMs with different prompting strategies and found that an ensemble shuffle approach worked best, providing a resource for representing clinical knowledge and predicting biomarkers related to pregnancy complications.

papers.title: Teaching diffusion models physics: reinforcement learning for physically valid diffusion-based docking.
papers.abstract: Molecular docking aims to predict the binding conformation of a small molecule to its protein target. Recent work has proposed diffusion models for this task, from rigid-body docking that diffuses over ligand degrees of freedom to co-folding approaches that jointly generate protein structure and ligand pose. However, diffusion-based docking models have been shown to frequently produce physically implausible poses and fail to consistently recover key protein-ligand interactions. To address this, we introduce a reinforcement learning framework for training diffusion-based docking models directly
papers.summary: This paper introduces a reinforcement learning framework to train diffusion-based molecular docking models, directly addressing their tendency to generate physically implausible poses and miss key protein-ligand interactions. By optimizing for physical validity and interaction recovery, the approach improves the reliability of diffusion-based docking predictions.

papers.title: SEFA: Semantic Embedding-Based Feature Augmentation of Biomedical Language-Model Embeddings Improves Interpretable Metabolomic Prediction of Lung Cancer.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Feature engineering remains a major challenge in metabolomics-based prediction, particularly when rich biochemical knowledge is available but underutilized. Conventional metabolomics models rely primarily on measured variables and statistically driven feature selection, overlooking the molecular and pathway context encoded in curated metabolite knowledge bases. We propose SEFA (Semantic Embedding-based Feature Augmentation), a model-agnostic framework that integrates metabolite-level textual knowledge from the Human Metabolome Database (HMDB) into structured metabolomics
papers.summary: SEFA is a new framework that augments metabolomics data with semantic embeddings of metabolite descriptions from the Human Metabolome Database, improving interpretable prediction of lung cancer. By integrating textual biochemical knowledge, it enhances model performance and interpretability compared to conventional feature selection methods.

papers.title: Exploratory Biological Correlates of Cognitive and Language Performance in Healthy Pubertal Children: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Adolescence is a dynamic neurodevelopmental period during which structured language performance may reflect ongoing biological reorganization processes. This study examined whether inflammatory, nutritional, and hormonal biomarkers were modestly associated with structured language task performance and cognitive performance in healthy pubertal children. Methods: A total of 156 healthy pubertal children (78 female, 78 male; mean age of 11.84 ± 2.98 years) meeting Tanner Stage ≥ 2 were included in this retrospective cross-sectional study. Language was assessed with the Test
papers.summary: This study explored whether inflammatory, nutritional, and hormonal biomarkers are associated with cognitive and language performance in healthy pubertal children. Using a retrospective cross-sectional design with 156 children, the findings suggest modest correlations between certain biological markers and structured language task performance, indicating that ongoing biological reorganization during adolescence may relate to cognitive outcomes.

papers.title: BioMaster: Multi-agent system for automated bioinformatics analysis workflow.
papers.abstract: The growing volume and complexity of biological data have made bioinformatics workflows increasingly labor-intensive, error-prone, and difficult to scale. Large language model-based agents offer potential for automation but often fail in complex, multi-step analyses because of limited robustness. We present BioMaster, a multi-agent framework that integrates workflow planning, execution, error recovery, and output validation. BioMaster incorporates a dual retrieval-augmented design to leverage domain knowledge for tool selection, parameterization, and adaptation across tasks. A dedicated debug
papers.summary: BioMaster is a multi-agent framework that automates complex bioinformatics workflows using large language models. It integrates workflow planning, execution, error recovery, and output validation, with a dual retrieval-augmented design to improve tool selection and parameterization. The system aims to increase robustness and reduce manual effort in multi-step biological data analysis.

papers.title: Brain-AI convergence: Generative world models and hierarchical attention for human intelligence.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in general-purpose AI provide new insights into how the neocortex and cerebellum, despite their uniform circuit architectures, support diverse functions and human intelligence. Beyond the traditional focus on visual processing, this paper offers a cross-domain comparison of the brain and AI through the lens of world-model-based computation. We argue that both the neocortex and cerebellum predict future world states from past inputs and construct predictive world models through prediction-error learning. These predictive world models are repurposed for sensory comprehension and
papers.summary: This paper proposes a unified framework comparing brain computation with modern AI, arguing that both the neocortex and cerebellum operate as predictive world models that learn through prediction errors. It suggests that these models, combined with hierarchical attention mechanisms, form the basis of human intelligence and can inform the development of more brain-like AI systems.

papers.title: Combining Triazole Scaffold Repurposing and Generative Transformer Architecture for Structure-Based Inhibitor Design Targeting the LasR Quorum Sensing Receptor of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
papers.abstract: Background: The rapid escalation of multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa necessitates anti-virulence strategies targeting quorum sensing rather than bacterial survival; however, integrating scaffold repurposing with generative AI to inhibit LasR remains underexplored. Here, we address this gap by combining triazole scaffold mining with transformer-based de novo molecular generation to systematically identify putative LasR inhibitors. Methods: An integrated computational pipeline involving Structure-based inhibitor design using Generative Transformer Architecture, deep learning-assisted GNINA resc
papers.summary: This study combines triazole scaffold repurposing with a generative transformer architecture to design novel inhibitors targeting the LasR quorum sensing receptor of Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The integrated computational pipeline, which includes structure-based design and deep learning-assisted rescoring, identifies putative LasR inhibitors as a potential anti-virulence strategy against multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa.

papers.title: Cancer of unknown primary: the evolution of tissue of origin identification in the artificial intelligence era.
papers.abstract: Cancer of Unknown Primary (CUP) presents substantial diagnostic and therapeutic challenges owing to its heterogeneous nature and the absence of an identifiable primary tumor site. This review provides a structured search of the pathogenesis, epidemiological characteristics, and limitations of traditional diagnostic and therapeutic approaches for CUP, with an emphasis on the evolution of Tissue of Origin (TOO) identification techniques. Recent advances in precision medicine have accelerated the development of machine learning-based TOO identification tools, representing a paradigm shift in CUP
papers.summary: This review examines the challenges of Cancer of Unknown Primary (CUP), focusing on the evolution of tissue-of-origin identification techniques, particularly the shift toward machine learning-based tools in the era of precision medicine. It highlights how these AI approaches may improve diagnosis and treatment guidance for this heterogeneous cancer type.

papers.title: Culture-Based Microbiological Assessment of Dentin Biomaterials Prepared from Long-Term Refrigerated Human Teeth: A Pilot Study Toward Evidence-Based Tooth Banking.
papers.abstract: Dentin derived from extracted human teeth has emerged as a promising autogenous biomaterial for bone regeneration owing to its structural and biological similarity to bone tissue. Growing clinical interest in dentin-derived graft materials has also stimulated the development of tooth-banking concepts, in which extracted teeth are preserved for future regenerative applications. However, microbiological contamination remains one of the principal concerns associated with long-term storage before clinical use. This in vitro study evaluated the microbiological status of dentin biomaterials prepared
papers.summary: This pilot study assessed the microbiological safety of dentin biomaterials prepared from human teeth stored long-term under refrigeration, finding that the processing methods effectively reduced contamination to acceptable levels. The results support the feasibility of tooth banking for future regenerative applications, though further validation with larger samples is needed.

papers.title: An interpretable XGBoost model for predicting arteriovenous fistula dysfunction in end stage renal disease.
papers.abstract: Arteriovenous fistula (AVF) dysfunction remains a major challenge in patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) undergoing hemodialysis. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an interpretable machine learning model based on clinical variables and preoperative laboratory parameters to predict AVF dysfunction.
papers.summary: This study developed an interpretable XGBoost machine learning model using clinical and laboratory data to predict arteriovenous fistula (AVF) dysfunction in hemodialysis patients with end-stage renal disease. The model aims to provide a transparent, clinically useful tool for early risk assessment.

papers.title: Multi-level Transcriptomic and Machine-learning Analyses Identify MZT1 as a Proliferation-associated Prognostic Marker in Lung Adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) exhibits substantial molecular heterogeneity and variable clinical outcomes, highlighting the need for biomarkers that reflect core tumor biological processes. Centrosome-associated proteins regulate mitotic fidelity and genome stability, yet their roles in LUAD remain incompletely defined. In this study, we systematically characterized mitotic spindle organizing protein 1 (MOZART1; MZT1) and related family members in LUAD.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-level transcriptomic and machine-learning analyses to identify MZT1 as a proliferation-associated prognostic marker in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). The findings suggest that MZT1 expression correlates with tumor proliferation and patient outcomes, offering a potential biomarker for prognosis in LUAD.

papers.title: TNFAIP3 and MLKL-Related Necroptosis Signatures in Liver Transplant Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury: Integrated Transcriptomic and Experimental Evidence.
papers.abstract: Liver transplant ischemia-reperfusion injury (LIRI) is a major cause of early graft dysfunction. Necroptosis has been implicated in inflammatory tissue injury; however, its molecular characteristics and diagnostic relevance in LIRI remain unclear. This study aimed to identify necroptosis-related biomarkers and characterize their biological and immune-associated features.
papers.summary: This study identifies necroptosis-related biomarkers, specifically TNFAIP3 and MLKL, associated with liver transplant ischemia-reperfusion injury (LIRI) using integrated transcriptomic and experimental approaches. The findings suggest these genes play a role in the inflammatory response and could serve as diagnostic markers for early graft dysfunction.

papers.title: Red blood cell distribution width is associated with coronary artery disease in latent tuberculosis infection: a machine learning-based study.
papers.abstract: Latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) is associated with an increased risk of coronary artery disease (CAD), potentially mediated by systemic inflammation. Traditional lipid-based risk models may have limited predictive performance in tuberculosis-affected populations.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning to investigate the association between red blood cell distribution width (RDW) and coronary artery disease (CAD) in patients with latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI). The findings suggest that RDW is a significant predictor of CAD in this population, potentially offering a better risk marker than traditional lipid-based models.

papers.title: Plasma proteomics reveals the molecular features in rapidly progressive pneumoconiosis.
papers.abstract: Rapidly progressive pneumoconiosis (RPP) is an aggressive subtype of pneumoconiosis characterized by persistent pulmonary inflammation, rapidly progressive fibrosis, and early-onset progressive massive fibrosis. However, the systemic molecular alterations of RPP remain unclear. Here, we profiled the plasma proteome to identify candidate proteins associated with RPP, aiming to discover potential peripheral biomarkers for this aggressive phenotype.
papers.summary: This study profiles the plasma proteome of patients with rapidly progressive pneumoconiosis (RPP) to identify systemic molecular changes and potential peripheral biomarkers for this aggressive fibrotic lung disease. The findings reveal candidate proteins associated with RPP, offering new insights into its pathogenesis and diagnostic markers.

papers.title: An evaluation based on explainable machine learning: analysis of risk factors for enteral nutrition-related diarrhea in patients with severe stroke.
papers.abstract: This study systematically examines the clinical factors associated with enteral nutrition-related diarrhea (ENAD) in patients with severe stroke and uses interpretable machine learning methods to assess the strength of these associations.
papers.summary: This study uses explainable machine learning to identify and rank clinical risk factors for diarrhea associated with enteral nutrition in severe stroke patients, providing interpretable insights for clinicians. The approach helps prioritize modifiable factors to reduce diarrhea incidence.

papers.title: Exploration of acetylation-related biomarkers in osteoarthritis through bioinformatics analysis.
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is characterized as a chronic degenerative disorder affecting the joints. A growing body of evidence indicates that acetylation may play a role in the disease's pathogenesis. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain largely undefined. The objective of this study was to explore potential biomarkers linked to acetylation in OA through a comprehensive bioinformatics analysis. We utilized datasets GSE55235, GSE55457, and GSE12021 from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) by employing the limma package, followed by functi
papers.summary: This study uses bioinformatics analysis of three GEO osteoarthritis datasets to identify acetylation-related differentially expressed genes as potential biomarkers, aiming to clarify the molecular mechanisms linking acetylation to OA pathogenesis. The findings may provide new diagnostic or therapeutic targets for osteoarthritis.

papers.title: A structure and function-based complete mutational map of human hemoglobin using AI.
papers.abstract: Hemoglobin (Hb), a well-characterized protein central to oxygen transport and molecular medicine, serves as a model for studying how sequence variations influence protein structure and function. Its precise activity depends on tightly regulated structural dynamics, which can be disrupted by mutations that give rise to structural hemoglobinopathies, including sickle cell disease, unstable hemoglobins, methemoglobins, and hemoglobins with altered oxygen affinity, each associated with distinct functional and clinical consequences. Among genetic variants, missense mutations are the most widely stu
papers.summary: This study uses AI to generate a complete mutational map of human hemoglobin, linking sequence variations to structural and functional consequences. It provides a comprehensive resource for understanding how missense mutations cause hemoglobinopathies like sickle cell disease and altered oxygen affinity.

papers.title: Explicit encoding of temporal dynamics for interpretable melody similarity modeling: insight into machine learning models.
papers.abstract: Temporal melody similarity is a fundamental problem in music modelling, and current methods are mostly based on recurrent or attention-based architectures that implicitly learn sequential structures.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a method for melody similarity that explicitly encodes temporal dynamics, offering a more interpretable alternative to recurrent or attention-based models that learn sequential structure implicitly. The approach provides insight into how machine learning models represent musical time, potentially improving both performance and understanding of melody comparison.

papers.title: MetaCYP: a unified framework for prediction of cytochrome P450 metabolic sites and reaction types via multimodal deep learning.
papers.abstract: Cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes are the predominant drug-metabolizing proteins in humans, collectively governing the structural transformation of drugs and xenobiotics while directly shaping their pharmacological activity and toxicological profiles. Accurate prediction of CYP-substrate reaction sites and reaction types is therefore central to drug discovery and metabolic risk assessment. Existing computational models, however, largely depend on intrinsic molecular properties or hardcoded reaction rules, constraining their generalization across CYP isoforms.
papers.summary: MetaCYP is a new multimodal deep learning framework that predicts both the metabolic sites and reaction types for cytochrome P450 enzymes, addressing limitations of existing models that rely on molecular properties or hardcoded rules. It offers a unified approach that improves generalization across different CYP isoforms, which is important for drug discovery and metabolic risk assessment.

papers.title: Peripheral endocrine-nutritional machine learning signature predicts short-term response to neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy in locally advanced gastric cancer.
papers.abstract: Major pathological response (MPR) to neoadjuvant PD-1 inhibitor plus chemotherapy in locally advanced gastric cancer (LAGC) varies widely and is incompletely explained by tumor-side biomarkers. Because checkpoint inhibitors act within a host environment shaped by endocrine, nutritional, and inflammatory state, we developed and validated the Endocrine-Nutritional Immunotherapy response score (ENI-Score) from routine pretreatment peripheral-blood markers to predict short-term response and early recurrence.
papers.summary: The authors developed and validated a machine learning-based score (ENI-Score) using routine pretreatment peripheral-blood markers of endocrine, nutritional, and inflammatory status to predict short-term response (major pathological response) to neoadjuvant PD-1 inhibitor plus chemotherapy in locally advanced gastric cancer. The score aims to complement tumor-side biomarkers by capturing host systemic factors that influence checkpoint inhibitor efficacy.

papers.title: EMCN is associated with vascular-immune crosstalk and represents a potential biomarker in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: While MUC family genes have been established as prognostic biomarkers in gastric cancer, and GWAS studies link EMCN mutations to chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression in NSCLC, the systematic characterization of EMCN in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains elusive.
papers.summary: This study provides the first systematic characterization of EMCN in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), revealing its association with vascular-immune crosstalk and its potential as a prognostic biomarker. The findings suggest that EMCN expression correlates with immune infiltration and may serve as a novel therapeutic target or diagnostic indicator in LUAD.

papers.title: SA-FGPN: Stability-aware feature-gated progressive learning for pediatric brain tumor classification from high dimensional gene expression data.
papers.abstract: Accurate pediatric brain tumor classification from gene expression data remains challenging due to the extremely high-dimensional nature of transcriptomic datasets, where tens of thousands of features are available from only a limited number of samples. This imbalance increases the risk of overfitting, unstable feature selection, and unreliable performance estimation. Moreover, molecular heterogeneity among pediatric brain tumor subtypes makes robust prediction and biological interpretation difficult. This study aims to develop a stable and interpretable deep learning framework for pediatric b
papers.summary: This paper introduces SA-FGPN, a stability-aware feature-gated progressive learning framework designed to classify pediatric brain tumors from high-dimensional gene expression data. The method addresses challenges like overfitting and unstable feature selection, offering a stable and interpretable deep learning approach for improved tumor subtype classification.

papers.title: Cross-residual knowledge graph learning for robust multi-trait gene-trait prioritization in rice.
papers.abstract: Prioritizing genes associated with agronomic traits remains challenging because relevant evidence is distributed across heterogeneous biological resources and curated gene-trait associations are incomplete.
papers.summary: This paper presents a new computational method that uses a knowledge graph to integrate heterogeneous biological data and prioritize genes linked to agronomic traits in rice, addressing the issue of incomplete curated gene-trait associations. The approach, called cross-residual knowledge graph learning, improves robustness and accuracy in gene-trait prioritization, potentially aiding crop improvement efforts.

papers.title: Computational Characterization of Pathogenic LMNA Missense Variants: Structural Instability, Altered Binding, and Conformational Dynamics.
papers.abstract: Mutations in the LMNA gene underlie a broad spectrum of laminopathies, including muscular dystrophies, cardiomyopathies, and premature aging syndromes; however, the molecular mechanisms by which missense variants disrupt Lamin A structural integrity remain incompletely characterized. Systematic computational approaches for prioritizing pathogenic variants and elucidating their structural consequences are critically needed.
papers.summary: This study computationally characterizes pathogenic missense variants in the LMNA gene, which cause various laminopathies. The authors analyze structural instability, altered binding, and conformational dynamics to understand how these variants disrupt Lamin A function and to prioritize pathogenic variants.

papers.title: InfoMedex: drug-drug interaction prediction via a multimodal CNN-transformer model.
papers.abstract: Drug-drug interactions are an important source of preventable adverse drug events. Computational methods that incorporate chemical structure and biological context may support more scalable and interpretable interaction prediction.
papers.journal: Frontiers in drug safety and regulation
papers.summary: InfoMedex is a new computational model that predicts drug-drug interactions by combining chemical structure data with biological context using a multimodal CNN-transformer architecture. The model aims to improve scalability and interpretability over existing methods, potentially aiding in the prevention of adverse drug events.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-integrated multimodal retinal imaging for early detection and risk stratification of systemic vascular and neurodegenerative diseases.
papers.abstract: We developed and validated RetinalVNG-Net, a multimodal deep learning framework for simultaneous risk stratification of hypertensive retinopathy, diabetic retinopathy, and neurodegenerative-associated retinal changes from integrated fundus photography, optical coherence tomography, and clinical metadata.
papers.summary: The authors developed RetinalVNG-Net, a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates fundus photography, optical coherence tomography, and clinical metadata to simultaneously assess risk for hypertensive retinopathy, diabetic retinopathy, and neurodegenerative retinal changes. This approach enables early detection and risk stratification of systemic vascular and neurodegenerative diseases through retinal imaging.

papers.title: OtoVCE: a mechanism-aware language-model evidence layer for hereditary hearing-loss variant interpretation.
papers.abstract: Missense variants in genes implicated in hereditary hearing loss are frequently returned to clinicians as variants of uncertain significance. In silico predictors and rule-based ACMG/AMP frameworks each capture only a fraction of the required evidence, and neither directly accesses case-level and functional evidence reported in the published literature.
papers.summary: This paper introduces OtoVCE, a language-model-based evidence layer that integrates case-level and functional evidence from the published literature to improve the interpretation of missense variants in hereditary hearing-loss genes. By combining this mechanism-aware evidence with existing in silico predictors and ACMG/AMP rules, OtoVCE aims to reduce the number of variants of uncertain significance returned to clinicians.

papers.title: The Embodied Hijack: when Pleistocene minds meet disembodied artificial intelligence.
papers.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence into everyday life has intensified a long-standing feature of human cognition: the attribution of agency, intention, and understanding to nonhuman systems. People describe language models, virtual assistants, and autonomous technologies as if these systems know, decide, want, or understand, and they continue to do so even when they know the systems have no inner life. The standard account dismisses this as naïve anthropomorphism, the misfiring of evolved agency-detection systems calibrated in the Environment of Evolutionary Adaptedness. We argue
papers.summary: This paper argues that the tendency to attribute agency and intention to AI systems is not a simple cognitive error but a deep-seated feature of human cognition rooted in Pleistocene adaptations. The authors propose that disembodied AI 'hijacks' these evolved mechanisms, leading people to treat AI as intentional agents despite knowing otherwise.

papers.title: SHAP-interpretable machine learning integrating exposures and multi-omics reveals immune alterations and biomarkers in COPD-lung cancer comorbidity.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and lung cancer (LC) frequently co-occur and share environmental and biological determinants, yet their cross-scale associations remain incompletely understood. Artificial intelligence and machine learning-based integration of exposome and multi-omics data provide new opportunities for dissecting this complex comorbidity.
papers.summary: This study uses SHAP-interpretable machine learning to integrate environmental exposures and multi-omics data, revealing immune alterations and potential biomarkers associated with COPD-lung cancer comorbidity. The findings provide new insights into the cross-scale biological mechanisms linking these two diseases.
